cues: The model to sit with is Cox regression. It says the hazard, the instantaneous risk of death, equals a baseline hazard times e to the beta times x. The baseline can be any shape. The covariates multiply it.
A hazard ratio above one means higher risk. Below one means lower risk.

In model A the one coefficient whose interval stays off one is recipient age: per five years, the hazard ratio is one point three three, with p equal to zero point zero two four. The other seven confidence intervals cross one.

Peripheral-blood stem cells lean protective, hazard ratio zero point seven zero, and the p-value is zero point two seven. A rank Schoenfeld test flags H L A mismatch at p equals zero point zero three four, so the reported fit stratifies on that covariate.

Training concordance is zero point six three. Five-fold cross-validation, with the imputer refit inside each fold, drops it to zero point five six, plus or minus zero point zero four. Model C is a ridge fit, penalizer zero point one, on the full standardized clustering matrix. It is there to check that coefficient signs agree.
